name: Governance & Operating Model
description: Decision rights, accountability and the forum structure that makes governance decisions binding rather than advisory. Defines who owns what data, who arbitrates conflicts, and what happens when a standard is breached.
buyerPain: Nobody can say who owns the number. Every disputed figure escalates to the CEO because there is no lower forum with authority to settle it.
coreArtefacts: Data Governance charter (signed by sponsor)
Target operating model — central vs federated split
Role definitions: Owner, Steward, Custodian
DG Council terms of reference and decision-rights matrix
Escalation and exception-handling procedure
Steward time-allocation letters countersigned by line managers
deliverables: DG charter approved at board or ExCo level
Named Data Owners per domain with signed accountability
Council constituted with quorum rules and first meeting held
RACI published across the governance lifecycle

bankingOverlay.focus: Aligns the DG council with existing bank governance so it inherits authority instead of competing with it — typically reporting into the Risk & Compliance Committee or the ALCO/Board Risk chain.
artefacts: Mapping of DG Council into existing bank committee hierarchy
CDO / Head of Data mandate letter
Alignment of data ownership to Basel risk-data accountability
Regulator-facing governance attestation pack
drivers: Internal audit findings on data ownership

name: Data Strategy & Business Alignment
description: Ties governance work to funded business outcomes. Without this pillar governance is a cost line that dies at the next budget cycle; with it, governance is a dependency of something the business already wants.
buyerPain: The last governance programme produced a policy binder and no measurable change, so finance will not approve a second one.
coreArtefacts: Data strategy on a page, aligned to the corporate strategy
Value hypothesis register with quantified pain (rework hours, findings, headcount)
Prioritised domain sequencing with rationale
Benefits-tracking model and baseline measurement
Governance business case with phased investment
deliverables: Quantified top-10 pain list with owner and baseline
Prioritised roadmap tied to funded initiatives
Business case with payback assumptions stated explicitly
Benefit baseline captured before wave 1 starts

bankingOverlay.focus: Anchors the strategy in the bank's regulatory calendar and AI agenda — the two budgets that are never cut. Governance is scoped as the enabling dependency of an already-funded programme.
artefacts: Regulatory submission calendar with data-dependency mapping
AI/GenAI readiness gap statement per use case
Cost-of-poor-data model: reconciliation FTE, report rework cycles, regulatory findings
Board KPI-to-data-element traceability
drivers: GenAI deployment blocked on data classification
M&A or core-banking migration due diligence

name: Data Architecture & Modelling
description: The structural layer — canonical models, integration patterns and the rules that stop each new system inventing its own version of 'customer'. Governance without architecture degenerates into per-report firefighting.
buyerPain: Every new system adds another customer table and another reconciliation job. Integration cost rises with each project instead of falling.
coreArtefacts: Conceptual and logical enterprise data model for governed domains
Canonical entity definitions and identifier strategy
Data architecture standards and integration patterns
System-of-record designation per subject area
Architecture exception register
deliverables: System-of-record map for all governed CDEs
Canonical model for the scoped domain
Architecture standards adopted into the project-approval gate
Duplicate-pipeline inventory with retirement plan

bankingOverlay.focus: Uses a banking industry logical model as the canonical reference so definitions are not invented from scratch — accelerates the modelling phase from months to weeks and gives regulators a recognised structure.
artefacts: FSDM-aligned subject-area map for governed domains
Core banking (CIF / accounts / GL) to canonical model mapping
Party, Arrangement, Event and Product entity alignment
Gap-extension register where the bank's products exceed the reference model
drivers: BCBS 239 Principle 2 (data architecture and IT infrastructure)

name: Metadata & Business Glossary
description: The shared vocabulary and the technical catalogue underneath it. This is the pillar that makes every other pillar addressable — you cannot govern, secure or classify what is not catalogued.
buyerPain: Three departments report 'active customers' and produce three different numbers, and no one can prove which definition is correct.
coreArtefacts: Business glossary with approved term definitions and synonyms
Technical metadata catalogue with automated harvesting
Term-to-physical-asset binding
Glossary approval workflow and change control
Metadata coverage and freshness metrics
deliverables: Glossary live with approved definitions for all governed CDEs
Catalogue ingesting metadata from the scoped source systems on schedule
Every CDE bound to its physical columns
Contested-term disputes resolved and recorded by the council

bankingOverlay.focus: Seeds the glossary from regulatory definitions rather than internal opinion — where the regulator defines a term, that definition wins and the debate ends.
artefacts: Regulatory term dictionary sourced from SBP return instructions
Pre-populated banking glossary (customer, exposure, NPL, restructured, stage-2, EAD)
Product hierarchy and Islamic banking term variants
Prudential vs management definition reconciliation notes
drivers: Conflicting figures between finance, risk and business
AI/RAG projects needing a semantic layer

name: Data Quality Management
description: Measurable rules bound to critical elements, executed on a schedule, published as a scorecard and worked through an issue-management workflow. This is the pillar that makes governance visible.
buyerPain: Quality problems are discovered by the recipient of the report, after it has gone out, and remediation is a fire drill every month-end.
coreArtefacts: DQ dimension framework (completeness, validity, accuracy, consistency, uniqueness, timeliness, integrity)
DQ rule library bound to CDEs
Profiling baseline per source system
DQ scorecard with thresholds and trend
Issue register with severity, owner and SLA
Root-cause and remediation workflow
deliverables: Executable rules running on schedule against every governed CDE
Published scorecard with a named owner per failing rule
Issue workflow live with triage SLA
Demonstrated defect-rate movement on at least five rules

bankingOverlay.focus: Ships a pre-written banking rule library rather than authoring rules from a blank page — the single largest accelerator in the whole engagement.
artefacts: Core banking DQ rule library across CIF, accounts, GL, cards, loans, collateral
Regulatory return reconciliation rules (GL-to-subledger, return-to-source)
IFRS 9 staging and provisioning data-quality rules
AML/CFT data-completeness rules for screening and reporting

name: Master & Reference Data
description: Single trusted versions of the entities that appear everywhere — customer, product, organisation unit, and the code sets that classify them. Reference-data drift is the quiet cause of most cross-system inconsistency.
buyerPain: The same customer exists five times across systems, so exposure aggregation, single-customer-view and cross-sell all give the wrong answer.
coreArtefacts: Master entity scope and survivorship rules
Match/merge strategy and stewardship queue for exceptions
Reference-data code-set register with ownership
Golden-record publication pattern to consuming systems
Duplicate-rate and match-confidence metrics
deliverables: Golden record defined and published for the priority master entity
Reference code sets registered with a named owner and change process
Stewardship queue live for match exceptions
Duplicate rate baselined and trending down

bankingOverlay.focus: Treats the customer master as a regulatory obligation rather than a marketing convenience — single-customer-view failures are directly examinable under exposure-aggregation and KYC rules.
artefacts: CIF de-duplication and single-customer-view rules keyed on CNIC/NTN
Related-party and group-exposure linkage register
Product and GL code-set governance
Branch/region hierarchy and organisational reference data

name: Lineage & Traceability
description: The ability to trace any published number back to its source fields and forward to every consumer. Lineage is both the defensibility artefact for regulators and the mechanism for deriving critical data elements.
buyerPain: When the regulator asks how a reported figure was derived, the answer takes three weeks and depends on one person who wrote the extract.
coreArtefacts: End-to-end lineage from source system to consumption point
Transformation documentation for each hop
Impact-analysis capability for proposed changes
Lineage coverage metric against governed CDEs
Manual-intervention register (spreadsheets, hand adjustments)
deliverables: Lineage captured for every governed CDE, source to report
Impact analysis demonstrably used in a real change request
Manual touchpoints identified and risk-rated
Regulator-presentable lineage evidence pack

bankingOverlay.focus: Runs lineage backwards from the regulatory return line item — this is simultaneously the CDE-derivation method and the audit-defensibility artefact.
artefacts: SBP return line-item to source-field lineage templates
GL-to-subledger-to-source reconciliation lineage
IFRS 9 ECL model input lineage
Spreadsheet and end-user-computing intervention register

name: Security, Privacy & Classification
description: Classification of data by sensitivity, the access model that enforces it, and the privacy obligations attached. This pillar has become the gating dependency for AI deployment.
buyerPain: We cannot let a model or a vendor touch the data because nobody can state, per column, what is confidential and who is entitled to see it.
coreArtefacts: Data classification scheme and labelling standard
Access model — role-based entitlements tied to data owners
Masking, tokenisation and de-identification standards
Privacy notice, consent and lawful-basis register
Third-party and cross-border data-sharing controls
Access recertification cycle
deliverables: Every governed CDE classified and labelled in the catalogue
Access requests routed through the data owner
Masking applied in non-production environments
Recertification run at least once with exceptions closed

bankingOverlay.focus: Combines banking secrecy obligations with emerging local data-protection expectations and the AI-vendor question that boards are now asking directly.
artefacts: Customer confidentiality classification aligned to banking secrecy obligations
PII and financial-sensitive column inventory across core systems
Cross-border processing and cloud residency assessment
AI/LLM data-exposure control statement per use case

name: Data Lifecycle & Retention
description: Governs data from creation through archival and defensible disposal, including the retention obligations that conflict with deletion rights and the storage cost of keeping everything forever.
buyerPain: Nothing is ever deleted, storage cost compounds annually, and legal cannot confirm what must be retained versus what should have been destroyed.
coreArtefacts: Retention schedule per data category with legal basis
Archival and disposal procedure with evidence of destruction
Data-sharing and egress register
Environment and copy inventory (how many copies exist and why)
Storage cost attribution by domain
deliverables: Retention schedule signed off by legal and compliance
Copy inventory produced with redundant copies identified
Disposal procedure executed once with evidence retained
Storage cost baseline attributed to owning domains

bankingOverlay.focus: Reconciles statutory record-retention periods against operational archival practice, which is usually far longer and far more duplicated than anyone has measured.
artefacts: Statutory retention mapping for account, transaction and KYC records
Dormant and unclaimed account data handling procedure
Legal-hold procedure for litigation and investigation
Core-banking archive and migration-era data disposition plan

name: Platform, Integration & Automation
description: The tooling substrate — catalogue, quality engine, lineage collection, orchestration — and the discipline of enforcing policy inside pipelines rather than inside documents.
buyerPain: A governance tool was purchased two years ago, is 8% populated, and nobody outside the DG team opens it.
coreArtefacts: Tooling reference architecture and integration map
Connector inventory and metadata-harvest schedule
Policy-as-code enforcement points in pipelines and CI
Deployment and environment topology
Adoption metrics — active users, coverage, freshness
deliverables: Catalogue, quality engine and lineage collector deployed and integrated
Automated harvest running on schedule for scoped systems
At least one policy enforced in a pipeline, not just documented
Adoption metric published and rising

bankingOverlay.focus: Assumes a constrained, on-premise-leaning bank environment with vendor core systems that expose metadata poorly — connector strategy matters more than tool brand.
artefacts: Core banking and CBS metadata extraction approach
On-premise deployment topology with network segregation
Warehouse and reporting-layer connector configuration
Change-management integration with the bank's release process

name: Analytics, AI & Consumption Governance
description: Governs what happens at the point of use — model inputs, feature provenance, report certification, and the controls that make AI deployment defensible rather than hopeful.
buyerPain: The board has asked for AI, and the honest answer is that we cannot certify what the model would be trained or grounded on.
coreArtefacts: Certified-report and trusted-dataset register
Model input and feature provenance documentation
AI use-case intake with data-risk assessment
Model monitoring for data drift on governed inputs
Consumption access and entitlement review
deliverables: Certified dataset register published with owners
AI intake process live with a data-readiness gate
Model inputs traced to governed CDEs
Uncertified shadow reporting inventoried and rationalised

bankingOverlay.focus: Directly addresses the 2026 board question — GenAI cannot be deployed on data that cannot be classified, traced or trusted, which makes governance the funded dependency of the AI budget.
artefacts: AI readiness assessment per candidate banking use case
IFRS 9 and IRB model input governance evidence
RAG corpus classification and access-control statement
Model risk management data-lineage evidence pack
drivers: Credit and fraud model input assurance
